1/6 Calling external contracts can transfer control to another contract before your function finishes.

2/6 This allows a malicious contract to call back into you, creating multiple invocations that interact undesirably.

3/6 The core risk is that state changes happen after the call, not before.

4/6 To prevent this, perform all internal state updates before making any external calls.

5/6 This approach is known as the Checks-Effects-Interactions pattern.

6/6 Alternatively, you can use a reentrancy lock like OpenZeppelin's ReentrancyGuard.
Review how your contract handles low-level call results, since unchecked failures may leave execution continuing without the intended effect
